    **10+. People of the land** (decided 21 October 2026). Each province's people in three groups, settled (with its men of fighting age counted apart), under arms and loose, with the flows between them ("People of the land"). Yield and levies come from the settled; battles, sieges, famine and plague count the dead and the runaways; births let a province recover slowly; disbanded men walk home, can be settled as colonists, and turn loose when disbanded far away; settled people move between neighbouring provinces of their kingdom towards room to spare, taking their share of the purse with them once item 9+a has purses ("Money moves with people"), refugees, and runaways from crushing taxes or hunger, cross borders as loose men, a king may settle newcomers in a province with room or return runaways under a tablet, and the loose drift freely ("Where people go" under "People of the land"); a conqueror may deport settled people from a province he has taken to one of his own ("Deportation"), and a besieged king may put out of the city the mouths that cannot fight ("People are worth having, not free to keep"); and the bands and banditry of item 11 draw on the loose, unpoliced loose men robbing a share of a province's purse and stores each season ("Bandits rob the purse"). The king's tax rate moves here from 9+a, so the lever comes with its consequence ("How a king lives"), and hunger answers in the season it bites: a hungry province loses some of its people that same season, to flight first, so the land's worth falls at once rather than a year later ("The wealth of a realm" under Victory). Yield then changes during a game, so scoring, levies and the script kings' calculations follow it, with the benchmarks recorded before and after. Each province's capacity comes from its land and climate, calibrated so that it starts at today's yield, and drought and flood follow its water, with one flood a year for each river shared along its course ("Land and climate" and "Rivers"); and the seasons by each province's climate, so levies at sowing and harvest cost more and armies abroad in a hard winter pay supplies ("Seasons"). In the pace rule, this item turns on water in arid land, fodder and the season on land ("What sets a company's pace"). First guesses, tuned in item 18. Built after item 10 and before item 11.

    **Built in two parts** (decided 21 October 2026), each its own pull request with its own stop for review, since the item has grown into two items' worth:
    - **10+a. People at home.** First, Haakon's answers to the reviews of items 9+a, 9+b and 10 (28 October 2026), where they differ from what was built: a mutinous unit's men keep what they carry and walk home with it like disbanded men, nothing reaching home before they do ("Soldiers carry savings home"); anyone's ships may bring grain to a besieged harbour while its waters are open, selling at what its market pays ("Stores and mouths are the clock"), in place of its king's ships only; a court knows a foreign market's prices and the tolls set on it only as last reported to it, never posted ("Tolls and smuggling"), in place of 9+b's half-season reach and posted tolls; model characters choose their own claims when they pitch and their own words when questioned ("Capture is questioning"), the formula serving script characters only; rumour travels by road at the pace of news, so far courts hear later; a false envoy is received in a full audience ("A false envoy"); and a captive handed over travels under guard like any company, so he can be intercepted or freed on the way. Then, by "Reason from the pillars" (under Overview): a false name exposed only by someone who has seen the man, a real envoy of the king he claims to serve, a letter to that king or an inquiry, never by chance alone; a sack's take and a breach's pace following their causes, the king's share of loot and a captured archive travelling home as loads that can be waylaid, instead of a third of the purse and the archive reaching the taker at once; every buyer at a market facing the same rising price, none fed first by the order the engine settles them in; a model character pitching from its belief, its skills as its self-assessment shows them ("Seeing oneself"), and choosing what to claim from it; each city's water set by where it stands, so a blockaded city holds no longer than its water ("Water too"); and harvests coming in each land's own season once land and climate come in this item. Then the three groups and the flows between them, births, disbanded men walking home or settled as colonists, settled people moving within their kingdom with their share of the purse, and the loose drifting; capacity from land and climate, drought, flood and rivers, and the seasons; the pace factors for water, fodder and the season; the king's tax rate, with hunger answering in the season it bites; every use of men drawing on the men of fighting age, at a cost that follows the season ("Settled" under "People of the land"); and yield changing during a game, with the benchmarks recorded before and after. With the men of fighting age come the people who defend their land ("The people defend their land"), in place of the walls a patron's gold buys a neutral city today, and the loose men's numbers following what the roads pay against what the land does ("Bandits rob the purse"). **Stop for review.**
    - **10+b. People across borders and in kings' hands.** Refugees and runaways crossing borders as loose men; settling newcomers and returning runaways under a tablet; deportation; putting the mouths that cannot fight out of a besieged city; and unpoliced loose men robbing a province's purse and stores. Built after 10+a. **Stop for review.**
